content_selection.rationale: The brief puts the right stories up front: Anthropic's disclosure about unintended eval actions, the White House statement on incident disclosure, OpenAI's misalignment reports, the withdrawn math manuscripts and the revenue correction. Cutting items already covered in earlier briefs, single-source rumors (Gemini 4 'Argon') and off-topic or minor items (Cloudflare–Deno, Colab perks, GGUF quants) was sensible. The clearest miss is Anthropic's 2026 Usage Policy update. It was widely covered and has no 'already covered' note, and it fits a brief that leads with Anthropic and governance far better than headline-only items built on truncated or paywalled sources, like the Manus round or the Apple order cut. NVIDIA's Nemotron result at IOI and IMO was a borderline cut that deserved at least a headline.
content_selection.evidence: Excluded: "Anthropic 2026 Usage Policy update (effective Nov 12; abuse of Claude, democratic processes)" with no 'already covered' note, while included items such as "Manus parent Butterfly Effect raises $500M+ (headline only; truncated source)" rely on thin sourcing.

selection_disagreements.story: Anthropic 2026 Usage Policy update (published Oct 8, effective Nov 12)
selection_disagreements.rationale: Coverage was broad: The Register, Notebookcheck, Unite.AI, AI Weekly and CryptoBriefing, and explainx.ai cites The Verge calling it Anthropic's first usage policy update in over a year. The changes matter: a new ban on sustained cruelty toward Claude, the blanket ban on personalized campaign targeting removed, tighter weapons-software and surveillance rules, and human review required for high-risk decisions like hiring and lending. The candidate list gives no sign an earlier brief covered it, and it fits a brief already leading with Anthropic and AI governance.

selection_disagreements.story: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 gold-level IOI 2026 (535.4/600, above top human) and IMO 2026 (30/42)
selection_disagreements.rationale: NVIDIA's Hugging Face post (Oct 7), picked up by several secondary outlets, reports an open-model system scoring above the best human at IOI 2026 (unofficial run) and gold-level at IMO 2026 with official graders, with checkpoints, datasets and pipeline released. It deserved at least a headline, especially since the brief already gives a long item to OpenAI's math claims and covers Western open-weight competition (Reflection, Mistral). The headline should flag that the IOI run was unofficial.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked the brief's main stories against live sources: the Anthropic eval incident, the White House SI Force statement, the OpenAI math withdrawals, the OpenAI revenue figures, Broadcom's chip financing, Nvidia–Reflection, Microsoft-Decision-1, Epoch's InnovationEval, OpenAI's grader misalignment report, Google's Gemini agent, Reflection's Beam and Australia's AI plan. Nearly every number, date and quote held up, and the brief hedged well on unconfirmed or vendor-run figures, such as the changed runner-up speed claim for Decision-1. I found no outright contradictions. Two attributions in the math story are off or unsupported, though. Retraction Watch names the advisory group as AGMAI (Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI), and I found nothing tying it to the Institute for Advanced Study. Retraction Watch also quotes Sutherland differently from the brief's paraphrase. A few smaller details, like police calling the delay 'unacceptable', I could not substantiate.
factual_accuracy.evidence: "roughly 50% of results were released without full formalization on the advice of the Institute for Advanced Study–linked advisory group" — Retraction Watch says the spokesperson credited the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI) and makes no mention of IAS.

length_format.rationale: Both counts sit at the top of the stated ranges: 15 Headlines bullets (target 8-15) and 10 deep-dives (target 5-10), split 1/3/2/1/3 across the five tiered sections, and the overall structure follows the template. The per-item length target of 3-6 sentences is often exceeded, though. About six of the ten deep-dives run 7-8 sentences, including the math, Broadcom, Nvidia/Reflection, Microsoft-Decision-1, InnovationEval and OpenAI misalignment items, and several individual sentences are long semicolon-chained run-ons. Some items also pad with tangential bundled material, such as the Mistral Large 4 recap folded into the Nvidia item and the Nadella post tacked onto the OpenAI item, so the brief is maxed out on counts and over-long per item.
length_format.evidence: The Nvidia/Reflection item runs about 8 sentences and bundles a second story: 'On the other Western open-weight bid, earlier briefs gave October 27 for Mistral Large 4's weights...'. The math item likewise appends 'Separately, Epoch AI's analysis of arXiv math preprints...' before its 'Why it matters' line.

dedup.rationale: Every story that overlaps a prior edition is explicitly flagged in today's brief, with the earlier dates named. Each of those follow-ups adds material new facts: the math withdrawals and formalization coverage, Broadcom's $50B+ credit specifics and the Anthropic debt guarantee, Nvidia's talks to acquire Reflection AI and Mistral Large 4's independent Vals score, and the new Microsoft-Decision-1 product. The remaining stories are absent from the Oct 7–9 editions: the Anthropic eval incidents, the White House disclosure statement, Australia's safety rules, OpenAI's misalignment reports, the revenue correction, the Gemini agent and InnovationEval. Nothing from the prior briefs, such as GPT-6, Haiku 5.5, Waymo, Ecosia, Isomorphic or the Cyber Mission, is repeated without a label.
